messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty → ALERT: prometheus:scrape_failures (job=\"scrape-exporter-prod\") firing for >90% targets failing. metric: prometheus_target_health{job=\"scrape-exporter-prod\"} count: 92/100 failed. severity: page. PD: https://pagerduty.example/INC12345 :rotating_light:

alex: acked oncall page. I'm looking — starting with target health + kube checks.

sam: confirmed grafana spike: https://grafana.example/d/abc123/log-ingest-overview — 5xxs up on /ingest endpoint and ingestion latency up ~3x for last 5m. Possible backlog.

alex: prometheus query: `sum by(instance)(up==0 and job==\"scrape-exporter-prod\")` => a bunch of exporter targets are reporting connection refused. running `kubectl get pods -n telemetry -l app=scrape-exporter -o wide` now.

alex: pods: scrape-exporter-12 CrashLoopBackOff, scrape-exporter-13 Running but failing healthchecks. Investigating logs: `kubectl logs -n telemetry scrape-exporter-12` shows repeated `dial tcp [10.0.45.78]:9100: connect: connection refused` error to a subset of nodes.

maya: @alex can you check k8s node conditions and whether kube-proxy on those nodes is flapping? also check iptables NAT table size, we've seen that cause scrape failures before.

alex: checking nodes: `kubectl get nodes -o wide` — two nodes showing NetworkUnavailable + kubelet NotReady briefly last 2m. ssh-ing to node-57.

alex: node-57 `dmesg` shows `br_netfilter: conntrack: nf_conntrack: table full` spikes. conntrack table at 65k, sysctl nf_conntrack_max=65536. That explains some connection refused.

luis: that will cause exporters to fail connections to endpoints and prometheus scrapes to time out -> log-ingest backlog likely grows. I'm checking kafka consumer group lag: `kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --describe --group log-ingest-consumers` shows lag ~1.2M messages across partitions.

sam: customer impact: noticing a few customers on real-time analytics reporting delayed events; our ingestion API returns 200 but internal processing lagging. Need quick mitigation to avoid dropping data.

oncall-bot: auto-escalation: PD escalated to SRE lead (englead) after 8m unacked by required role.

englead: on it. prioritize clearing backlog and preventing further scrape load. if we reduce scrape frequency or disable noisy exporters temporarily we can let consumers catch up.

maya: two immediate actions: 1) increase nf_conntrack_max on affected nodes (sysctl) and trigger rolling restart of kube-proxy on those nodes; 2) throttle or disable non-critical Prometheus scrape jobs to reduce new load.

alex: applying sysctl on node-57 and node-58: `sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144` — applied. restarting kube-proxy: `kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart daemonset/kube-proxy` (targeting nodes 57/58 first).

ops-runbook-bot: runbook: NetworkConntrackOverflow — recommended nf_conntrack_max bump and restart kube-proxy; temp disable high-churn exporters. Link: https://runbooks.redwood/network/conntrack-overflow

alex: kube-proxy restarted on node-57 and node-58; monitoring conntrack count — dropping from 65k to 30k. exporters starting to reconnect.

maya: while that propagates, i'm going to patch PrometheusServiceMonitor for `scrape-exporter-prod` to reduce scrape_interval from 15s to 120s for non-critical targets. Command: `kubectl patch servicemonitor scrape-exporter-prod -n telemetry --type='merge' -p '{"spec":{"endpoints":[{"interval":"120s"}]}}'`

alex: done patch. also disabled a couple of noisy exporters (kube-state-metrics-debug) `kubectl label svc kube-state-metrics-debug telemetry/monitoring-disabled=true --overwrite` — prometheus scrape config excludes labeled services.

luis: scaled log-consumer deployment: `kubectl scale deployment/log-consumer -n ingest --replicas=8` — pods coming up. consumer lag now ~900k and dropping.

sam: :thumbsup: early signs good — 5xxs on /ingest reduced from 4.2% -> 1.1% in last 10m. ingestion latency trending down.

alex: Prometheus scrape_failures metric now 28/100 failed instead of 92/100. Grafana panels show scrape_success ratio improving.

incident-bot: PD update: incident INC12345 acknowledged by alex, status: mitigated -> in progress.

englead: good progress. next: we should fully restore nf_conntrack max across cluster via daemonset and update terraform, revert temporary scrape changes only after stability for 1h. assign follow-ups.

maya: creating follow-up tasks: (1) infra: persistent nf_conntrack bump & node image check — @luis (2) monitoring: revert scrape interval and add exporter churn alert threshold — @sam (3) runbook: add conntrack overflow to Prometheus runbook — @alex

luis: taking infra task. will open infra PR to set sysctl via machine-config + add node-level alert for conntrack utilization > 70%.

alex: last check: log consumer lag at 120k and dropping, scrape_failures 8/100. pushing a status update to PD and customer ops.

sam: posting customer-facing note to ops channel: "We are mitigating increased ingestion latency due to node-level connection table saturation; expected to be resolved within 30-60m. No data loss expected. Will update as we know more." :eyes:

maya: once stable we should run a controlled replay of any retained messages to verify end-to-end.

alex: final: will keep eyes for 30m then mark resolved. I created incident ticket INC12345 with timeline + actions. Postmortem owners: alex (detection & mitigation), luis (infra fix), sam (alerts/runbook).

ops-runbook-bot: reminder: add links to playbook and prometheus queries used: `sum by(job)(scrape_series_added_total)` and `prometheus_target_health` for follow-up doc.

englead: thanks team. good coordination. please capture all commands in incident doc and open PRs for infra changes.

alex: marking this thread: incident mitigated at 3332113476. will update channel with postmortem link when ready. :white_check_mark:
